title: Build intake harness for open-source model weights with deterministic validation and telemetry
creator: Ethan Zhang
description: Scope: Implement a resilient intake harness that runs deterministically on newly submitted open-source model weights, performs conversion/normalization, runs a battery of validation and sanity checks, executes a small profiling pass to generate an initial performance profile, and emits telemetry and artifacts that feed the pin/recommendation system. Goals: 1) Detect corrupt or incompatible weight bundles early (checksum + manifest verification + signature detection). 2) Convert common formats (HF PyTorch, safetensors, torchscript) into our canonical runtime format with deterministic outputs. 3) Run deterministic functional smoke tests (token-level matching on a small prompt set) and KV-cache correctness checks. 4) Run a short profiling pass (few inference traces) to publish initial latency and memory estimates and a suggested pin (quantized and full precision variants). 5) Produce traceable artifacts for auditing and model governance: conversion log, deterministic-diff, profiling JSON, and a pin suggestion record. Tradeoffs considered: - Full exhaustive profiling costs too much early, so we limit to representative sequence lengths (16, 128, 1024) and a small batch matrix. - Deterministic checks accept small tolerated numerical drift thresholds for quantized variants (tolerance configurable per-model). - Prefer fast conversion path (safetensors -> runtime blob) but keep a slower fallback if model uses custom ops. Acceptance criteria: - New harness runs end-to-end on a submitted weights bundle, producing a conversion artifact and a profile JSON stored under model artifacts. - Deterministic smoke tests pass within configured tolerances for at least one quantization profile when applicable. - Output includes a recommended pin string (model:version:variant) and a confidence score. - Telemetry events emitted to Grafana/Influx (ingest.latency, convert.time, smoke.success, profile.latency_estimate, pin.recommendation) for dashboards and alerts. - Playbook updated with recovery steps and known failure modes.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Ethan Zhang: Initial write-up and scope. Tagged Asha for implementation. Referenced existing onboarding templates and the artifact gateway design.

2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Spike completed. Verified conversion path for HF safetensors and PyTorch .pt. Found two failure modes: non-standard module naming and custom operator namespaces. Added fallback to run a model-graph sanitizer that renames ambiguous modules.

2025-02-14 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested the harness produce a human-readable conversion log and include a link to the canonical model card in metadata. Also asked for pin confidence computation (score between 0-1).

2025-02-17 - Marco Ruiz (Security): Flagged need for signature/ownership verification for weights from community sources. Added mandatory manifest signature check step and KMS verification for private uploads. Security review required before shipping.

2025-02-19 - Asha Patel: Implemented deterministic smoke runner and KV-cache correctness tests. On quantized path saw 0.7% token-level average divergence on llama-variant at 1024; configured tolerance to 1.0% for q4_* profiles. Opening PR for conversion toolchain: https://github.com/redwood-inference/weights-converter/pull/114

2025-02-22 - SRE (review): Noted intermittent failures on conversion worker due to disk IO spikes during large weight unpacking. Action: throttle parallel unpacking and add disk pressure alert. SRE created an infra ticket ENG-82800 to track worker autoscaling tweaks.

2025-02-25 - Asha Patel: Profiling harness integrated. First automated profile produced for community/phoenix-7b: latency 12ms (@seq=128, batch=1, V100), memory 13.2GB, recommended pin: community/phoenix-7b:2025-02-25:fp16 with confidence 0.82. Pushing artifacts to staging bucket and publishing profile to model registry for review. Next: add more systematic sequence-length coverage and extend pin-recommendation logic to consider cost-per-token estimates.
next_steps: Stabilize conversion worker under disk pressure (coordinate with ENG-82800)
Add multi-sequence profiling runs and cost-per-token estimator integration
Implement manifest signature verification UI in console and surface warnings
Wire pin recommendations into the pinflow service and add an audit trail
